title: Oldest Light
hook: Blur the oldest light in the universe.
sub: A 48-degree patch of NASA WMAP's cosmic microwave background under an 18-qubit quantum blur, a stand-in for a telescope's blurry eye: watch which ripples survive.
you_control: Drag Mapper the satellite across the sky to wipe between the original and its blurry view
Slide the blur through 6 real engine strengths and watch its eye go fuzzy
Plant galaxy seeds on the hottest spots: count which ones the blur keeps, loses or invents
Switch quantum / Gaussian beam / COBE 7-degree view, flip Scene / Data, then take the quiz
qubits_note: 257 x 257 grid -> each axis padded to 512 -> 9 + 9 = 18 qubits (documented rule; every job's status also reports 'Recovered 18-qubit grid from measurement'). Sky fills 25% of the 2^18 amplitudes. 24/22/21 qubits refused by the 1 MiB request limit (free probes); 20 qubits failed for sibling pieces; our 19-qubit job 89f0fcee ran then failed on the platform's result-size limit (TMPRL1103).
honesty: Real NASA WMAP 9-year ILC data; the quantum blur is an analogy for telescope resolution (not a model of inflation), run on Atlas's classical statevector simulator, with all classical steps labelled.
